neighbours.label: The time-horizon or stage word inside an adverbial 'in the ___ term/run/stages' (long, short, early, immediate), vs the same adjectives as ordinary modifiers of a concrete noun
fire: Raising prices might help sales today, but in the long run customers will leave.
Most skin cancers can be cured when they are found in the early stages.
Their budget looks fine, at least in the short term, according to the auditors.
Aid workers said the greatest danger in the immediate aftermath was disease.
Analysts warned that, in the longer term, the mine would exhaust the aquifer.
Doctors say the drug works best when given in the early days of the illness.
Building more roads only eases traffic in the short run, planners argue.
Nobody knows whether the treaty will hold up in the long term, she wrote.
quiet: Hikers crossed the long bridge over the gorge before sunrise.
Most mornings she catches the early train to the city centre.
After lunch we took a short walk along the canal.
The immediate family gathered at the house after the funeral.
Engineers replaced the longer cable with a lighter one.
The early settlers built their cabins along the river bank.
He wore a short jacket and a pair of old boots.
A long line of cars waited at the border crossing.
